Tom — thanks, and appreciate the diagram. Below is a condensed 'activation readiness' checklist you can run through; I kept it targeted for day-0 handoff so your ops/procurement teams can parallelize work.

=== Redwood Private: Day-0 Activation Readiness (compact) ===
1) Account & Procurement
   - Confirm signed MPA (Master Private Arrangement) and billing contact.
   - Provide preferred maintenance window(s) and blackout dates.
2) Networking & Connectivity
   - Provide CIDR ranges for peering/routing (primary and failover).
   - Confirm egress requirements (required external endpoints & ports).
   - NAT gateway plan (if using on-prem NAT vs. cloud egress).
   - If using direct interconnect, share VLAN/peer details and ASN.
3) Identity & Secrets
   - KMS/HSM details: vendor, key wrapping policy, and contact for cert exchange.
   - Service account list (names + least-privilege roles) — see sample below.
4) Host & Admin Access
   - Jumpbox/Bastion IP(s) or secure VPN endpoint for initial validation.
   - List of admin users (name + corporate email) for one-time onboarding.
5) Observability & Security
   - Syslog/siem endpoint and log retention expectations.
   - Any inbound allowlist for our control-plane callbacks (URLs/ips).
6) Validation Evidence
   - Test SSH (port/host) and sample API call success criteria.
   - Small smoke test prompt set and expected latency targets.

Sample service account table (example):
- redwood-deployer@sentinel (compute: create, read; network: view)
- redwood-secret-agent@sentinel (kms: use, wrap; logs: write)

Notes/constraints:
- For KMS: we support common HSM vendors and key wrap via RSA/EC; we cannot import keys without a wrapped key exchange. If you need Redwood to generate and rotate keys, flag that now.
- Control-plane callbacks must be reachable from listed egress IPs; we can provide a CIDR block to allowlist.

Next steps I suggest:
- Laura can own the cert/KMS exchange and Ben will coordinate the network validation runbook.
- If you can return the service account list + CIDRs by Tue (2026-11-24), we can schedule a provisioning window the following week.

Thanks — attaching a short runbook template for the activation window.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Network smoke test and access checklist — Redwood <> Sentinel

Tom — attaching the concise network validation steps you can run with your ops team prior to our provisioning window. High level: verify peering, confirm control-plane callback reachability, and run a tokenized request against our staging endpoint.

Quick steps (executed from your jump host):
1) Verify BGP/peering (if using direct interconnect) — confirm routes for Redwood CIDR 10.30.0.0/16
2) TCP probe: nc -vz redwood-callback01.prod.redwood.com 443 (expect: open)
3) HTTPS probe: curl -i -H 'x-rdwd-test: sentinel' https://redwood-callback01.prod.redwood.com/healthz
4) KMS connectivity: tls-handshake to HSM endpoint and validate accepted ciphers

We will provide a short-lived API key for the smoke test; it expires 72 hours after issuance. Mina will validate logs and respond with a pass/fail matrix.

Ben Carter
Senior Network Eng, Redwood Inference
